title: How music, memory and emotion are connected, with Elizabeth Margulis, PhD

sentences.en: Are there songs that take you back in time?
sentences.zh: 有没有哪首歌能让你瞬间回到过去？

sentences.en: Maybe that summer anthem that played endlessly the year you were 16, or the first dance from your wedding, or even an ad jingle from childhood.
sentences.zh: 也许是16岁那年循环播放的夏日金曲，或是婚礼上的第一支舞，甚至只是童年里的一段广告配乐。

sentences.en: Whatever it is, hearing even a snippet of the right music can transport us back decades and make us feel the emotions we felt back then.
sentences.zh: 无论是什么，哪怕只是听到一小段熟悉的旋律，都能让我们穿越回几十年前，重温当时的心境。

sentences.en: Today we're going to talk about why that happens and the many ways that music, memory, emotion, and imagination intertwine.
sentences.zh: 今天我们要探讨这种现象背后的原因，以及音乐、记忆、情感和想象力之间千丝万缕的联系。

sentences.en: So why do some songs make us happy or sad?
sentences.zh: 那么，为什么有些歌会让我们感到快乐或悲伤？

sentences.en: Why do some give us chills and others make us want to dance?
sentences.zh: 为什么有些音乐会让我们起鸡皮疙瘩，而有些却让我们想跳舞？

sentences.en: Why do some pieces of music transport us back in time?
sentences.zh: 为什么有些乐曲能带我们穿越时空？

sentences.en: Is there a reason that people are especially attached to music from their teenage years?
sentences.zh: 人们对青少年时期的音乐情有独钟，这背后有什么原因吗？

sentences.en: How do our culture and our expectations affect the way we experience music?
sentences.zh: 我们的文化和预期又是如何影响我们对音乐的体验的？

sentences.en: And finally, why are we so drawn to some songs that we want to listen to them over and over again,
sentences.zh: 最后，为什么我们会被某些歌曲深深吸引，以至于想一遍又一遍地听，

sentences.en: yet when other songs get stuck in our heads, we call them earworms and they drive us slightly crazy?
sentences.zh: 而当其他歌曲在脑海中挥之不去时，我们却称之为“耳虫”，甚至觉得有点抓狂？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association that examines the links between psychological science and everyday life.

sentences.en: I talked a moment ago about how the right song can transport us back to a particular time or a moment in our life.
sentences.zh: 刚才我提到，合适的歌曲能把我们带回生命中的某个特定时刻。

sentences.en: Why is that?
sentences.zh: 这是为什么呢？

sentences.en: Why is music so strongly connected to memory?
sentences.zh: 为什么音乐与记忆的联系如此紧密？

sentences.en: People have been fascinated by this question for ages.
sentences.zh: 长期以来，人们一直对这个问题着迷。

sentences.en: And in fact, it's not only music that people suspect to have this power.
sentences.zh: 事实上，人们怀疑具有这种力量的不仅仅是音乐。

sentences.en: So think of the famous Madeleine in Proust, where you take a bite or smell something from your childhood, suddenly all kinds of vivid details come back to you.
sentences.zh: 想想普鲁斯特笔下那块著名的玛德琳蛋糕，当你咬上一口或闻到童年的某种气味时，各种生动的细节会瞬间涌上心头。

sentences.en: So because there are other sensory stimuli that can have a similar effect, one of the first questions people have asked is,
sentences.zh: 由于其他感官刺激也能产生类似的效果，人们提出的首要问题之一就是：

sentences.en: is there really anything special about music when it comes to autobiographical memory?
sentences.zh: 在自传体记忆方面，音乐真的有什么特别之处吗？

sentences.en: And one of my favorite studies on that topic was conducted by Amy Belfi.
sentences.zh: 我最喜欢的相关研究之一是由Amy Belfi进行的。

sentences.en: And what she did was compare the autobiographical memories that were prompted by hit songs from specific years versus famous faces that
sentences.zh: 她所做的是比较由特定年份的热门歌曲引发的自传体记忆，与那些在同一年份

sentences.en: had a lot of airtime in those same specific years.
sentences.zh: 高频出现的著名面孔所引发的记忆。

sentences.en: The idea is they're both kind of similarly repeated and kind of in circulation at a particular time.
sentences.zh: 其理念是，两者在特定时期都被反复提及，且处于同样的传播环境中。

sentences.en: So she just show people the face or play people a bit of the song and ask them whether it triggered some memory from their life.
sentences.zh: 她只是向人们展示面孔或播放一段歌曲，然后询问这是否触发了他们生活中的某种记忆。

sentences.en: And if so, to describe it.
sentences.zh: 如果是，就请他们描述出来。

sentences.en: And she found indeed that the music produced especially vivid kind of memories.
sentences.zh: 她发现，音乐确实能产生特别生动的记忆。

sentences.en: So people had more kind of descriptive language, more sensory detail.
sentences.zh: 人们使用了更多的描述性语言，包含了更多的感官细节。

sentences.en: It was really coming back in a more lifelike way than it was for simply the prompt of a visual image and a face.
sentences.zh: 与单纯的视觉图像或面孔提示相比，音乐带来的回忆确实更加栩栩如生。

sentences.en: So it really seems to be a real phenomenon.
sentences.zh: 所以这似乎是一个真实存在的现象。

sentences.en: So why do so many people get especially attached to music from their teen or young adult years?
sentences.zh: 那么，为什么许多人对青少年或青年时期的音乐情有独钟呢？

sentences.en: I mean, most of us aren't wearing the same clothes or reading the same books that we did back then, but we're still listening to the same music.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们大多数人现在穿的衣服、读的书都和那时不同了，但我们依然在听当时的音乐。

sentences.en: from looking at the other eras of our life that function similarly.
sentences.zh: 那就是观察我们生命中其他具有类似功能的时期。

sentences.zh: 有大量证据表明，这可以触发记忆改善，并具有有趣的临床潜力。

sentences.en: But in fact, uh, lots of research shows that even very basic things about, um, uh, how, how a
sentences.zh: 但事实上，大量研究表明，即使是关于某个特定和弦听起来如何，

sentences.en: particular, um, chord sounds or how a particular collection of, um, pitches sounds, you think
sentences.zh: 或者某组音高听起来如何这样非常基础的事情，

sentences.en: varies according to the kind of exposure that you've had within your life and the musical systems that you've been, um, kind of trained up on in terms of your ear.
sentences.zh: 也会根据你一生中的接触经历以及你耳朵所受过的音乐系统训练而有所不同。

sentences.en: So, so we're really finding that this, uh, prescription for universality is really not there in exactly the way that our
sentences.zh: 所以我们发现，这种对普遍性的定义，并不完全像我们的直觉有时所暗示的那样。

sentences.en: intuition would sometimes suggeSt. On the other side of the same coin, what about music that's considered universally ugly or unpleasant?
sentences.zh: 反过来说，有没有被认为普遍丑陋或令人不悦的音乐？

sentences.en: I'm thinking about like during the Renaissance, right?
sentences.zh: 比如我想到了文艺复兴时期，对吧？

sentences.en: The Catholic church forbade the use of the augmented fourth, which they called diabolus musica.
sentences.zh: 天主教会禁止使用增四度，他们称之为“音乐中的魔鬼”。

sentences.en: What was it about this particular chord that got people so riled up?
sentences.zh: 这个特定的和弦究竟有什么特别之处，让人们如此愤怒？

sentences.en: And is there music that's universally considered ugly for want of a better descriptor?
sentences.zh: 有没有什么音乐被普遍认为是丑陋的（如果用词不当的话）？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So people think a lot about, um, dissonance, about notes that you play them together and they kind of sound grating or they don't sound sweet and sonorous, um, together.
sentences.zh: 人们对不协和音思考很多，即当你把音符放在一起演奏时，它们听起来很刺耳，或者听起来不够甜美悦耳。

sentences.en: And there've been a, there's a big history of psychoacoustic explanations.
sentences.zh: 心理声学解释有着悠久的历史。

sentences.en: Like think about Pythagoras, this idea that there's something about the physical property of resonating bodies that, um, there's a long history of people thinking,
sentences.zh: 想想毕达哥拉斯，他认为共鸣体的物理属性中存在某种东西，长期以来人们一直认为，

sentences.en: oh, there's these small special kind of numeric relationships between pitches that sound good together.
sentences.zh: 哦，音高之间存在着某种微小而特殊的数字关系，让它们听起来很和谐。

sentences.en: And that's why they sound good.
sentences.zh: 这就是它们听起来好听的原因。

sentences.en: And this is like, must be kind of a baked in feature.
sentences.zh: 这一定是一种与生俱来的特征。

sentences.en: Um, whereas we now know, for example, uh, with work by Josh McDermott and Nora Jacoby, Melinda McPherson,
sentences.zh: 然而我们现在知道，例如，通过Josh McDermott、Nora Jacoby和Melinda McPherson的工作，

sentences.en: they worked with people in rural Bolivia called the Chimane who don't have a lot of music that is, um, has multiple voices going on at once.
sentences.zh: 他们与玻利维亚农村的奇马内人合作，他们没有太多同时包含多个声部的音乐。

sentences.en: So usually it's kind of one melody at a time.
sentences.zh: 所以通常一次只有一段旋律。

sentences.en: And, uh, they basically made a bunch of songs for them, taking these melodies and adding another line
sentences.zh: 他们基本上为他们创作了一堆歌曲，采用这些旋律并添加了另一条声部，

sentences.en: so that you had either a very sweet sounding consonant kind of series of sounds or a quite
sentences.zh: 这样你就会得到一系列听起来非常甜美的协和声音，或者相当...

sentences.en: grating dissonant series of sounds that was like, you know, either a dissonant accompaniment to this melody that was quite familiar to them or a consonant, um, accompaniment.
sentences.zh: 刺耳、不和谐的一连串声音，就像是，你知道，要么是给他们非常熟悉的旋律配上不和谐的伴奏，要么是和谐的伴奏。

sentences.en: And, uh, the Chimane had no trouble whatsoever noting that these were different kinds of accompaniments.
sentences.zh: 而且，奇马内人（Chimane）完全能轻易分辨出这些是不同类型的伴奏。

sentences.en: Like you could categorize those ones, you know, kind of go together.
sentences.zh: 就像你可以把那些归类，你知道，它们听起来比较协调。

sentences.en: These ones that sound sweet, these ones that sound grating kind of go together, but there was absolutely no difference for them in terms of which they liked or found pleasurable.
sentences.zh: 那些听起来悦耳的，那些听起来刺耳的，它们各自归为一类，但对他们来说，在喜欢或觉得愉悦的程度上，完全没有区别。

sentences.en: Like truly they tested so many different ways.
sentences.zh: 他们真的尝试了非常多种不同的方式。

sentences.en: There was just nothing about a consonant accompaniment that they liked or enjoyed any more than a dissonant, uh, accompaniment.
sentences.zh: 对于和谐的伴奏，他们并没有比不和谐的伴奏表现出更多的喜爱或享受。

sentences.en: Um, yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯，是的。

sentences.en: And I mean, I, uh, like I have a range of, of friends with such varied musical tastes, including people who swear that they can't get their children to sleep without playing,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我，嗯，我有各种各样的朋友，他们的音乐品味非常不同，包括那些发誓说如果不给孩子放，

sentences.en: you know, death metal.
sentences.zh: 你知道，死亡金属音乐，他们就没法让孩子入睡的人。

sentences.en: Like, you know, there's just, it's to, to each their own.
sentences.zh: 就像，你知道，这只是，萝卜青菜，各有所爱。

sentences.en: Um, yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯，是的。

sentences.en: What about exposure to music across cultures?
sentences.zh: 那么跨文化的音乐接触呢？

sentences.en: I mean, like it's almost like food, you know, in some cultures you would eat a kind of food, which in America we wouldn't like.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这就像食物一样，你知道，在某些文化中你会吃某种食物，而在美国我们可能不喜欢。

sentences.en: And there's music that comes from the East that may sound dissonant to our ears, where our music may sound dissonant to Eastern ears.
sentences.zh: 有些来自东方的音乐在我们的耳朵听来可能是不和谐的，而我们的音乐在东方人的耳朵听来也可能是不和谐的。

sentences.en: I mean, how does this come about or is it what, is it a matter of what we're exposed to in our youth, what becomes acceptable and consonant to us?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是怎么形成的？或者说，这是否取决于我们在年轻时接触了什么，什么对我们来说变得可以接受且和谐了？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: It's very similar to what happens in language acquisition.
sentences.zh: 这和语言习得中发生的情况非常相似。

sentences.en: So if you look at little tiny babies, um, and what they're able to detect in terms of phonemes, um, in terms of like the basic units of language, there's a lot they can do
sentences.zh: 所以如果你观察那些小婴儿，嗯，观察他们能检测到的音素，嗯，也就是语言的基本单位，他们能做的事情有很多，

sentences.en: before they specialize and prune their abilities and become little experts in their own language.
sentences.zh: 在他们专门化、修剪自己的能力并成为各自语言的小专家之前。

sentences.en: So an example would be, um, distinguishing between the sounds of R and L, but in some other languages there, those sounds are kind of together in one category.
sentences.zh: 举个例子，嗯，区分 R 和 L 的发音，但在某些其他语言中，这些声音被归为同一类。

sentences.en: Um, and so depending on the kind of exposure baby has, they'll either kind of develop this ability to separate different kinds of
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以根据婴儿接触到的语言类型，他们要么会发展出这种能力，将不同的，

sentences.en: continuous changes on the spectrum from R to L into two different binary categories, um, or not.
sentences.zh: 从 R 到 L 频谱上的连续变化，区分成两个不同的二元类别，嗯，要么就不会。

sentences.en: And, uh, you really see this ability develop or, or, I mean, you, another way of thinking about that is they lose the ability to make that distinction.
sentences.zh: 而且，嗯，你确实能看到这种能力的发展，或者，我的意思是，另一种思考方式是，他们失去了做出那种区分的能力。

sentences.en: Um, if they're, uh, if that distinction is not relevant in their language and we see the same thing with music.
sentences.zh: 嗯，如果他们，嗯，如果那种区分在他们的语言中不相关，我们在音乐中也看到了同样的情况。

sentences.en: So there've been great studies with babies using special kinds of musical meters.
sentences.zh: 所以已经有很棒的研究针对婴儿使用了特殊的音乐节拍。

sentences.en: Um, so most of the songs that we hear, um, in on the radio, let's say in the States, uh, are going to be like in two or in three groups of, you know,
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以我们听到的大多数歌曲，嗯，在收音机里，比方说在美国，嗯，都会是两拍子或三拍子，你知道，

sentences.en: beats that are in groups of two or three, these kinds of simple meters.
sentences.zh: 节拍以二或三为一组，这些简单的节拍。

sentences.en: Um, so they're evenly divided.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以它们是均匀划分的。

sentences.en: Whereas in other styles, so Balkan folk music, for example, it's very common to have meters that are in five or seven.
sentences.zh: 而在其他风格中，比如巴尔干民间音乐，五拍子或七拍子是非常常见的。

sentences.en: You have uneven groups.
sentences.zh: 你有不均匀的组合。

sentences.en: You have like three followed by two and then three and then two.
sentences.zh: 比如三拍子后面跟着两拍子，然后是三拍子，然后是两拍子。

sentences.en: Um, and that's, that's very unfamiliar for, uh, other kinds of musical styles.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这对其他类型的音乐风格来说是非常陌生的。

sentences.en: So babies, it turns out, start out, you know, it's no problem for them.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，婴儿一开始，你知道，这对他们来说没问题。

sentences.en: They don't care if it's like a group of five or a group of two or a group of seven, they're like equally good at all of them.
sentences.zh: 他们不在乎是五拍子、两拍子还是七拍子，他们对所有这些都同样擅长。

sentences.en: But then you keep raising them in the U S or Canada or something.
sentences.zh: 但后来你继续在美国或加拿大等地抚养他们。

sentences.en: And, um, they lose that ability by like 12 months old.
sentences.zh: 而且，嗯，他们在 12 个月大左右就会失去那种能力。

sentences.en: They don't know what's going on with the five, uh, you know, the groups of music that's in groups of five or seven.
sentences.zh: 他们不知道五拍子，嗯，你知道，那些五拍子或七拍子的音乐是怎么回事了。

sentences.en: But what's cool is you can, um, resurrect that ability really easily.
sentences.zh: 但很酷的是，你可以，嗯，非常容易地恢复那种能力。

sentences.en: Uh, so researchers just gave them the parents CDs of some Balkan folk music, sent them home and said, you know, over the course of a week, just occasionally play this CD.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以研究人员只是给了父母一些巴尔干民间音乐的 CD，让他们带回家，并说，你知道，在一周的时间里，偶尔播放一下这张 CD。

sentences.en: Um, they did that.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他们照做了。

sentences.en: And then the babies back, like no problem.
sentences.zh: 然后婴儿们又恢复了，就像没问题一样。

sentences.en: So just passive exposure to certain kinds of sonic patterns is enough to, um, support the development of that ability at that age.
sentences.zh: 所以，仅仅是被动接触某些声音模式就足以，嗯，支持那个年龄段该能力的发展。

sentences.en: It's not so easy.
sentences.zh: 这并不容易。

sentences.en: If you try to do the same thing in an adult, it takes a lot more exposure and a lot more kind of like explicit training to regain an ability that you lost when you were a kid.
sentences.zh: 如果你试图在成年人身上做同样的事情，就需要更多的接触和更多明确的训练，才能重新获得你在小时候失去的能力。

sentences.en: So there's lots of, um, parallels there to what it's like to try to learn a language when you're older versus when you're a kid, um, really similar kinds of sets of processes.
sentences.zh: 所以这和你在成年后尝试学习语言与小时候学习语言的过程有很多相似之处，嗯，真的是非常相似的过程。

sentences.en: So there are areas in the brain for speech and smell and hearing.
sentences.zh: 所以大脑中有负责语言、嗅觉和听觉的区域。

sentences.en: Is there a music area in our brain?
sentences.zh: 我们的大脑中有音乐区吗？

sentences.en: That's a question that animated a lot of research for a lot of time.
sentences.zh: 这是一个长期以来激发了大量研究的问题。

sentences.en: And the answer really seems to be no.
sentences.zh: 而答案似乎确实是否定的。

sentences.en: In fact, it seems to be that what's so amazing and special about music is that it draws on so many other different abilities and so many other different, um, parts of your brain.
sentences.zh: 事实上，音乐之所以如此神奇和特别，似乎是因为它利用了许多其他不同的能力和大脑中许多其他不同的部分。

sentences.en: So if you think about, uh, what's needed to just perform or even listen to and make sense of and be moved by music, there's these motor aspects, motor control,
sentences.zh: 所以如果你思考一下，嗯，仅仅是表演，甚至只是聆听、理解并被音乐感动需要什么，这里有运动方面，运动控制，

sentences.en: um, regions about, in fact, even if you passively listen to music, it turns out you rely on motor areas of your brain to process music that has a beat.
sentences.zh: 嗯，区域，事实上，即使你只是被动地听音乐，事实证明你也会依赖大脑的运动区域来处理有节拍的音乐。

sentences.en: There's this very tight connection between the auditory and the motor system.
sentences.zh: 听觉系统和运动系统之间存在着非常紧密的联系。

sentences.en: Um, you need to have a cognitive faculty, right?
sentences.zh: 嗯，你需要具备认知能力，对吧？

sentences.en: To be able to process and evaluate the sounds and make sense of how they relate to one another.
sentences.zh: 能够处理和评估声音，并理解它们之间是如何关联的。

sentences.en: Um, to make sense of what the song might be about, you have to have some kind of empathetic or emotional kind of sense.
sentences.zh: 嗯，要理解歌曲的内容，你必须具备某种共情或情感上的感知。

sentences.en: There's really, it just starts combining so many different things, which is one reason that people
sentences.zh: 它确实开始结合了这么多不同的东西，这也是人们，

sentences.en: look to musical training as, um, you know, a resource for scaffolding and all kinds of other abilities across the course of development.
sentences.zh: 将音乐训练视为，嗯，你知道，在整个发展过程中支撑各种其他能力的一种资源的原因之一。

sentences.en: So if there's no musical center in the brain, how do we understand what happens to people say who were never musical in their lives,
sentences.zh: 所以如果大脑中没有音乐中心，我们该如何理解那些人身上发生的事情，比如那些一生中从未接触过音乐的人，

sentences.en: have a head injury and can suddenly play Beethoven?
sentences.zh: 头部受伤后突然能演奏贝多芬的作品？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: There are all kinds of, um, oddities of that sort.
sentences.zh: 这类奇怪的事情有很多。

sentences.en: One is tone deafness.
sentences.zh: 一个是音盲。

sentences.en: Um, where, in fact, this is, this is kind of an interesting phenomenon because, you know, as I'm talking now, I bet a certain percentage of people listening are like, that is me.
sentences.zh: 嗯，事实上，这是一种有趣的现象，因为，你知道，当我说话时，我敢打赌一定比例的听众会想，那说的不就是我吗。

sentences.en: I am definitely tone deaf.
sentences.zh: 我绝对是音盲。

sentences.en: Um, but in fact, lots of people who think they're tone deaf deaf are really not.
sentences.zh: 嗯，但事实上，许多认为自己是音盲的人其实并不是。

sentences.en: Um, because if someone's truly tone deaf, the standard is that the test for assessing that, um, involves listening to a melody and then you listen to the same melody and one note
sentences.zh: 嗯，因为如果一个人真的是音盲，标准是评估它的测试，嗯，包括听一段旋律，然后你听同样的旋律，其中一个音符，

sentences.en: is like super off and people who are tone deaf cannot hear, they don't know if the melodies were
sentences.zh: 非常离谱，而音盲的人听不出来，他们不知道旋律是否，

sentences.en: the same or not, but it's, it's completely obvious to anyone who is not tone deaf that those are not the same.
sentences.zh: 相同，但对于任何不是音盲的人来说，这完全显而易见，它们是不一样的。

sentences.en: Often, you know, someone who claims they're tone deaf, it's totally apparent to them that something dramatic has changed.
sentences.zh: 通常，你知道，一个声称自己是音盲的人，他们完全能察觉到有什么剧烈的变化。

sentences.en: What makes them think they're tone deaf is that they have trouble singing, which can be, um, a production problem, like a problem with controlling your voice to match
sentences.zh: 让他们认为自己是音盲的原因是他们唱歌有困难，这可能是，嗯，一种产生问题，比如控制你的声音以匹配，

sentences.en: kind of what you hear versus a perception problem, which is what tone deafness is.
sentences.zh: 你所听到的声音的问题，而不是感知问题，而音盲正是感知问题。

sentences.en: And this kind of goes for the whole kind of range of special skills and special deficits related to music is that it has
sentences.zh: 这适用于与音乐相关的各种特殊技能和特殊缺陷，即它与，

sentences.en: to do with, um, little sub parts and components and ways things are connected, right?
sentences.zh: 小的子部分、组件以及事物连接的方式有关，对吧？

sentences.en: So you can get these interesting dissociations where, for example, somebody loses the ability to produce speech,
sentences.zh: 所以你可以得到这些有趣的解离，例如，某人失去了产生语言的能力，

sentences.en: like they have aphasia, um, but they've preserved the ability to sing, for example.
sentences.zh: 比如他们患有失语症，嗯，但他们保留了唱歌的能力，例如。

sentences.en: And, um, that seems mysterious.
sentences.zh: 而且，嗯，这看起来很神秘。

sentences.en: Like why, uh, could someone not be able to say the sentence, I lost my book, um, but can sing Mary had a little lamb, you know, with no problem whatsoever.
sentences.zh: 就像为什么，嗯，有人不能说出“我丢了我的书”这句话，嗯，却能毫无问题地唱出《玛丽有只小羊羔》，你知道。

sentences.en: So there's a whole kind of way of, uh, treating aphasia or addressing it that, um, relies on the preserved ability to sing where people
sentences.zh: 所以有一种治疗失语症的方法，嗯，依赖于保留下来的唱歌能力，人们，

sentences.en: gradually kind of scaffold in more speech-like, um, kind of utterances on top of the song that they're still able to produce.
sentences.zh: 逐渐地在他们仍然能够产生的歌曲之上，加入更多类似语言的，嗯，话语。

sentences.en: Um, yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯，是的。

sentences.en: So, so I guess what I'm saying in response to your initial question is that, uh, there's, there's a whole, you know, complex interconnected world.
sentences.zh: 所以，所以我想我对你最初问题的回答是，嗯，有一个，你知道，复杂且相互关联的世界。

sentences.en: So you can just snip out or, or kind of damage any kind of one part of it.
sentences.zh: 所以你不能只是剪掉，或者，嗯，损坏其中的任何一部分。

sentences.en: And there's like compensatory things that arise in another area or, you know, some specific symptom that appears, but, um, it's not kind of characterizing your
sentences.zh: 在另一个区域会出现补偿性的东西，或者，你知道，出现某种特定的症状，但是，嗯，它并没有表征你的，

sentences.en: performance overall, but is maybe just affecting one bit of how you perform musically.
sentences.zh: 整体表现，而可能只是影响了你音乐表现的一小部分。

sentences.en: The thing about like that you mentioned, which is people, these tales of people who've had a stroke or
sentences.zh: 关于你提到的那件事，也就是人们，那些中风或，

sentences.en: something, and then become incredibly interested in music and just produce a ton of music.
sentences.zh: 其他情况后，变得对音乐极其感兴趣并创作了大量音乐的故事。

sentences.en: I think there's a really interesting kind of thing there that has to do with motivation and interest, which is
sentences.zh: 我认为那里有一件非常有趣的事情，与动机和兴趣有关，这，

sentences.en: increasingly acknowledged as a key part of musicality.
sentences.zh: 越来越被公认为音乐性的关键部分。

sentences.en: Let me give you a couple of examples here.

sentences.zh: 嗯，所以随着人们开发出那些真正能够衡量，嗯，人们最初有多大音乐性的工具，关于他们对音乐有多少兴趣，

sentences.zh: 当我刚开始进入这个领域时，占主导地位的模型都与语言有关。

sentences.zh: 但音乐中有一个部分就是无法融入那个范式。

sentences.en: And that was how kind of ludicrously repetitive music is because there's just almost no circumstance in conversation

sentences.en: or, you know, other kinds of ordinary language uses where you would repeat yourself to the degree that music ordinarily does.

sentences.en: And, um, you know, we seem to like it, right?
sentences.zh: 而且，嗯，你知道，我们似乎喜欢它，对吧？

sentences.en: The chorus comes back several times in the song, but like, that's not enough.
sentences.zh: 副歌在歌中反复出现几次，但，那还不够。

sentences.en: Um, in fact, to a degree that sometimes I think people, um, fail to kind of acknowledge themselves and like when their Spotify wrapped appears at the end of the year and they
sentences.zh: 嗯，事实上，达到了一种有时我认为人们，嗯，没有意识到自己的程度，比如当他们年底的 Spotify 年度总结出现时，他们，

sentences.en: see, they listen to, you know, Radiohead's specific song, like you get 800 or 20 times or something.
sentences.zh: 看到他们听了，你知道，Radiohead 的特定歌曲，比如你听了 800 或 20 次之类的。

sentences.en: It's a little bit, uh, sobering, but it really seems like that's an important part of how music works for us.
sentences.zh: 这有点，嗯，令人清醒，但这确实看起来是音乐如何为我们工作的重要部分。

sentences.en: We string together these chains of what happens.

sentences.zh: 我们能够在脑海中把它唱出来。

sentences.en: We have this sense of participating, uh, along with it that seems to be important.
sentences.zh: 我们有一种参与其中的感觉，嗯，这似乎很重要。

sentences.en: Um, and so I really wanted to look at repetition and figure out, you know, what it was doing and
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以我真的很想研究重复，并弄清楚，你知道，它在做什么，

sentences.en: were kind of like stressed out or embarrassed with that repetitive and we're like trying and maybe not make a big deal out of it.
sentences.zh: 当时有点，嗯，对重复感到压力或尴尬，我们就像试图不去大惊小怪。

sentences.en: But sometimes songs that we don't want to think about get stuck in our heads, right?

sentences.zh: 有一些证据表明，我们之所以会进行某种心理重演，通常是为了

sentences.en: So another, this is kind of a terrifying thought that you might, there might be lots of earworms percolating, uh, in, you know, your mental landscape.

sentences.en: There's only some of them that kind of, uh, pop up into consciousness and, um, that you, you actually recognize.
sentences.zh: 只有其中一部分会浮现在意识中，并且是你真正能意识到的。

sentences.en: Um, but yes, there are definitely certain songs that tend to be particularly catchy.
sentences.zh: 嗯，是的，确实有些歌曲往往特别洗脑。

sentences.en: And I mean, it's not the same for everyone necessarily.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这对每个人来说不一定都一样。

sentences.en: Like people,
sentences.zh: 比如有些人，

sentences.en: I've known people who are big classical music heads that can get like a Brahms symphony theme stuck in their head, but typically it's these, you know, really, really catchy songs.
sentences.zh: 我认识一些古典音乐发烧友，他们脑子里会一直回荡着勃拉姆斯的交响乐主题，但通常情况下，还是那些非常、非常洗脑的歌曲。

sentences.en: You think of like, um, Carly Rae Jepsen's call me, maybe people talk about that one a lot, you know, and then there's like really terrible ones.
sentences.zh: 你会想到像卡莉·蕾·杰普森的《Call Me Maybe》，人们经常谈论那首歌，当然还有一些非常糟糕的歌。

sentences.en: Like the, it's a small world after all the plays in the Disney world, ride.
sentences.zh: 比如迪士尼乐园游乐设施里播放的《It's a Small World》。

sentences.en: And, and there's lots of evidence about what causes something to pop up as an earworm.
sentences.zh: 关于是什么导致某段旋律成为“耳虫”，有很多证据。

sentences.en: Um, it helps if it's quite singable kind of song, straightforward in a tempo that you can kind of like, um, move along with easily.

sentences.en: There's something a little unusual that you kind of get up on or get stuck, uh, get stuck about.
sentences.zh: 有一些稍微不寻常的地方，让你能记住或者被它困住。

sentences.en: It's actually something interesting you can do is the next time you have a song stuck in your head, really think back.

sentences.en: And it turns out when people try to figure out what prompted it, they're often quite good at it.

sentences.en: Like it's, it had some literal kind of prompt.

sentences.en: Um, they're also contagious because, uh, this happens in my household all the time that somebody doesn't really realize they have a song stuck in their head.

sentences.zh: 我可以给你放一首歌，你给我放一首歌，我们脑海中浮现的意象往往是一样的，我认为大多数人可能不会预料到这一点。

sentences.en: And it's pretty fun.
sentences.zh: 这很有趣。

sentences.en: How do visual images affect our reaction to music?
sentences.zh: 视觉意象如何影响我们对音乐的反应？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Um, I, I think they're, they're huge.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为它们的影响非常巨大。

sentences.en: It turns out, um, you know, even if we just, we've, we've done these studies where we've just asked people after we play them something,
sentences.zh: 事实证明，嗯，你知道，即使我们只是，我们做过这些研究，在播放完音乐后问人们，

sentences.en: what'd you think about while you're listening to that?

sentences.en: They could say, they could be like,
sentences.zh: 他们可能会说，他们可能会说，

sentences.en: Oh, I was thinking it was too loud or like, Oh, I was thinking I needed a sandwich or, you know, they could say anything.

sentences.en: And, um, the most common things they end up saying are like picturing some kind of fictional story, picturing like a movie, remembering something that really
sentences.zh: 而且，他们最终说的最常见的事情是想象某种虚构的故事，想象一部电影，回忆起真正

sentences.en: happened to them, um, visual imagery.
sentences.zh: 发生在他们身上的事情，嗯，视觉意象。

sentences.en: So all these things that are these like imaginative kind of remembered responses.
sentences.zh: 所以所有这些都是这种富有想象力的回忆式反应。

sentences.en: And I think this is one of the ways we zone out frequently in a very pleasant way.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是我们经常以一种非常愉快的方式“放空”的方法之一。

sentences.en: When we're listening to music, it sort of enables us to coast on it or, or daydream in, um, this way that can be very, uh, satisfying.
sentences.zh: 当我们听音乐时，它使我们能够顺着它滑行，或者以一种非常令人满足的方式做白日梦。

sentences.en: And in fact, where a lot of the, our emotional response to music might come from, right.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我们对音乐的许多情感反应可能就是由此而来的，对吧。

sentences.en: It might not be like exactly that the sound itself is cuing an emotion.
sentences.zh: 可能并不完全是声音本身在触发某种情绪。

sentences.en: It could be rather that the sound is cuing some specific image, or it's cuing some memory.
sentences.zh: 更有可能是声音在触发某种特定的意象，或者它在触发某种记忆。

sentences.en: And that image or memory is cuing the emotion.
sentences.zh: 而那个意象或记忆正在触发情绪。

sentences.en: Um, and I think that's really something that's happening a lot more than we might expect.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为这确实比我们预期的要发生得多。

sentences.en: Given these almost universal connections between music and, and certain emotions, how effective is music as a therapeutic device?
sentences.zh: 鉴于音乐与某些情绪之间几乎普遍存在的联系，音乐作为一种治疗手段有多有效？

sentences.en: There's so much interesting work in that space right now.

sentences.en: And then there was like research about them.
